evidence: Full bhalla explicitly lists Bengali bhāla, Oriya bhala/bhalā and Assamese bhāl “good”, with regional short and long vowels. These eastern survey forms continue that good-adjective family. Turner calls the shortening irregular and compares bhadra through *bhadla; the family link retains that qualification and leaves regional borrowing unresolved.

Full tanu/tanuka explicitly includes Hindi tanuk/tanak/tanik “small”. The selected few/quantity responses preserve that whole adjective, with source vowel length and internal transcription space retained; the ordinary small-to-few use is compatible with the entry’s Pali thin/small senses. Longer -yākā and nīkanā forms are not reduced to this stem.

Full nikta gives its Middle Indo-Aryan replacement *nikka, Lahnda nikkā “small, young”, Khetrani nikṛā and Western Pahari nikṛo “small”. Both members of each selected Awankari slash response belong to this same nikkā/nikṛā family, so the complete response is covered; mixed nikkā plus choṭā/nanḍā responses remain excluded.
